newsitem.title: ITALY: "Earthlings need nourishment" -- the summit quotes.
newsitem.headline: "Earthlings need nourishment" -- the summit quotes.

text.p: The World Food Summit ended at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) headquarters on Sunday after five days of speeches.
The following is a taste of what was said at a meeting that pledged to halve world hunger within 20 years.
"Before the eyes of the world you made a public commitment. I hope we will never forget our commitment." Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi in closing comments.

"Together we will work hand in hand to ensure that young children and babies will not cry of hunger and that mothers will not be looking at children who have no hope." -- FAO Director General Jacques Diouf.
"There are some very nice things written in the Declaration, but it is wishful thinking" -- Viplab Halin, Calcutta Institute for Motivating Self Employment NGO.
"Human rights and respect for democracy must not be seen as luxuries to be enjoyed only by those who can afford them" -- Irish Prime Minister John Bruton.

"The rich do not know hunger...What kind of cosmetic solutions are we going to provide so that in 20 years from now there would be 400 million instead of 800 million starving people? The very modesty of these goals is shameful." -- Cuban President Fidel Castro.
"We must put aside the sophist view that when there are many, one is condemned to be poor" -- Pope John Paul.

"I for one think that implementing action plans for the benefit of our fellow human beings must be at the top of all our agendas, not more summits. We have had enough of them." -- British Overseas Development Minister Lynda Chalker.
"Hunger is not an inevitable condition of man, it is something we can do something about" -- Danish Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen.
"Hunger and malnutrition are a scourge, a curse that cannot be tolerated any longer, morally, socially, politically or economically" -- European Union Commissioner Franz Fischler.

"Earthlings need nourishment much more than any Martians," Frank Lui, prime minister of the South Sea island of Niue, telling the summit that money spent on sending space probes to Mars would be better spent on food closer to home.
"Eat your veggies, not your friends" -- slogan used at a vegetarian demonstration involving a man dressed as a carrot.
"We should not have to wait until people are dying...to have a Robin Hood policy. The world is not Sherwood Forest" -- Diouf.
"I certainly earned my pay today," U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman after three women stripped naked during his news conference to protest against genetically altered soybeans.
"We are trying to find out exactly where the speaker is in the text that is in front of the interpreter," apology during Hebrew speech by Israel's Agriculture Minister Rafael Eitan.
"That we had to convene here from all ends of the earth to participate in a World Food Summit surely constitutes a severe rebuke for all of us" - Thabo Mbeki, South African Deputy President.
